result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend a stepper for travelers and radio cards for room type, and both argue well for showing all options when people need to compare rooms. A covers rubric item 3 a little better because it accepts a plain select for travelers as a v1 fallback. B covers mobile a little better, with the 16px text size, the numeric keypad, and its point that eight radios are clunky on a phone. Each answer also has one unsupported claim: A says most bookings are for 1–4 travelers, and B cites a '2–7 range' rule. The strengths and weaknesses roughly balance out. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give clear recommendations for each field: a stepper for travelers and radio cards for room type. Both also justify keeping the room options visible. B is slightly ahead on the number range: it says a plain select for travelers is a fine first version and that native selects work well on mobile, while A only argues for a stepper. B also covers accessibility and capacity rules in more detail, and A says it has 'one tweak' but never says what it is.
